title: Unique normalized strict-system second slot shift
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an arbitrary scheme W and an integer r. There exists exactly one natural isomorphism moving the shift r in the strict-system second slot to a shift of the tensor output, satisfying systemTensorRightProperty of [def-pur-integral-tensor-shift-properties]. The normalization is required on every resolving pair, with no condition that l be invertible on W. Uniqueness is equality of the natural isomorphisms, not merely existence of an isomorphism between their endpoints.

proof.text: Use Mathlib CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₂Iso for the actual sheaf tensor, with the independent-universe monoidal and additive instances. Its summand equation, evaluated on the sheafification unit applied to a pure tensor, is precisely systemTensorRightFormula after commuting r*i. Naturality in both variables is the map₂CochainComplex shift square.

For an acyclic test F and K-flat Q, Tot(F tensor Q) is acyclic. Its shift is acyclic, and the signed cochain isomorphism identifies it with Tot(F tensor Q[r]); hence shifts preserve K-flatness. Conjugate the localized signed cochain comparison by the recorded natural tensor-model isomorphisms and the canonical Q shift isomorphism. This gives a natural isomorphism on the full subcategory of K-flat pairs with exactly the prescribed normalization.

K-flat resolutions give every complex a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex. Extend the normalized comparison in each variable by exists_natTrans_from_resolvingClass on the homotopy category and descend through Qh using fully faithful whiskering. Fullness of the homotopy quotient proves naturality on the resolving class. The extended transformation is invertible because it is invertible on resolutions; their localized augmentation maps and the essential surjectivity of Q transfer this to every object. Extend first in the second variable; equality of natural transformations is detected on resolving objects, giving naturality in the first. Then extend in the first variable and uncurry.

Cancel the initial tensor of the Q shift isomorphism to verify the required model equation on each K-flat pair. For uniqueness, sheafification adjunction and sectionwise tensor generation imply that maps out of a tensor summand agree if they agree on every pure section. Totalization hom extensionality therefore makes the two cochain isomorphisms in the normalization equal. Cancel the invertible input shift map in the two model equations to get equality of the derived components on K-flat pairs. Each derived object is isomorphic to the localization of a K-flat resolution; naturality along the two representative isomorphisms gives equality on every pair. Natural transformation and isomorphism extensionality finish.
